title: Liked list memory freeing issue/memory leak
body_html:

             temp1 = Temp_Val[i];

    for ( i = A ; i >= 0 ; i--){
      node = malloc(sizeof(Node));

      node->key1 =  Temp_Key1[i];

      }

    printf("\n");

}

events.body_html:
Your loops are wrong:

for (i = 0; i<A ; i++ ){
   if (Temp_Key1[i] < Temp_Key1[i+1]){

but for i is A-1, there is no Temp_Key1[i+1], i.e, there is no Temp_Key1[A].

The same for your loop

for ( i = A ; i >= 0 ; i--){
    node->value = Temp_Val[i];

there is no Temp_Val[A].

Just change to

for (i = 0; i<A-1 ; i++ ){

and

for ( i = A-1; i >= 0 ; i--){
Nowhere in the code you've shown is any sort of assignment made to any Node::next value, which free_list is accessing.
Hello thanks for your comment. Unfourntantly it didnt work, it still had the same issue
rearranging a linked list is modifying the contents of the next (and if doubly linked, prev) pointer(s) There is no need to be calling malloc() nor free().
Please post the struct definition of each node in the linked list

regarding: the function signature: void free_list(Node * head){ at some point, the head pointer needs to be set to NULL. To do that the code needs to pass a pointer to a pointer to head. however, the code fails to do that
the posted code does not compile! Please post a minimal reproducible example so we can reproduce the problem and help you debug it.
